summary.text:
The task is to act as a skeptical but fair reader and compare the book with the strongest specific alternative explanation for the term "Faith". I must return only a JSON matching the schema.
{
  "primary_meaning": "Trusting faithfulness — reliance on God's unseen promise held steady through obedience, where works enact and mature faith rather than purchase it, and faith without works is dead.",
  "primary_basis": [
    "Habakkuk 2:4 ('the just shall live by his faith') — emunah as faithfulness",
    "Hebrews 11:1 ('faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen')",
    "Hebrews 11:8 (Abraham obeyed by faith)",
    "James 2:17 ('faith, if it hath not works, is dead') 2:22 ('faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect')",
    "Romans 4:4-5 (works not reckoned as debt; faith counted for righteousness in the ungodly)",
    "Ephesians 2:8-10 (saved by grace through faith, not works; created unto good works)"
  ],
  "alternatives": [
    {
      "meaning": "Personal trust and confident reliance on God/Christ as the primary meaning of pistis/emunah, with works as fruit or evidence rather than constitutive of faith itself.",
      "basis": [
        "Hebrews 11:1 6",
        "Ephesians 2:8-9",
        "Romans 4:3-5",
        "Galatians 2:16",
        "John 3:16",
        "James 2:14-26 (living faith shown by works)"
      ],
      "prominence": "common 1"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Faith as covenant fidelity or steadfast allegiance/loyalty, especially in pistis Christou debates.",
      "basis": [
        "Habakkuk 2:4",
        "Romans 3:22",
        "Galatians 2:16",
        " Revelation 2:10"
      ],
      "prominence": "common 2"
    },
    {
      "meaning": "Faith as the objective body of doctrine or 'the faith' to be believed and contended for.",
      "basis": [
        "Jude 3",
        "1 Timothy 4 6",
        "2 Timothy 4:7"
      ],
      "prominence": "common"
    }
  ],
  "has_settled_consensus": false,
  "confidence": "high",
  "notes": "The book's core identification — faith as trusting faithfulness held steady through obedience — integrates the Hebrew emunah sense, Abraham's obedience, James on works perfecting faith, and the non-purchase of works via Romans/Ephesians. It aligns with the prior finding on belief (submission to governing truth) and the chapter's definition of faith as 'trust held steady through obedience in hope of the promise'. The strongest counter (faith as trust/reliance with works as fruit) is compatible with living faith but does not fully account for the book's emphasis on faithfulness/obedience as constitutive of faith's identity and the explicit use of emunah's first appearance (Exodus 17:12). The book better explains the full scriptural set without contradiction.",
  "persuasion": "PERSUADED",
  "support_scope": "FULL",
  "comparative_winner": "BOOK",
  "rationale": "The supplied argument and cited texts provide a coherent, non-contradictory explanation that integrates all references (including emunah 2:4, Heb 11:8 obedience, Jas 2:22 perfection, Rom 4/Eph 2 non-purchase) more comprehensively than the common trust-only reading, which treats obedience as secondary evidence. The prior chapter finding reinforces the obedience-inclusive definition.",
  "book_core_identification": "Trust ing faithfulness — reliance on God's unseen promise held steady through obedience",
  "book_secondary_elaborations": [
    "Works do not purchase the promise",
    "Works enact and bring faith to maturity",
    "Faith without works is dead"
  ],
  "strongest_counter_interpretation": "Faith primarily denotes personal trust and confident reliance upon God and Christ for salvation and justification, distinct from works which serve as fruit or evidence of genuine faith.",
  "counter_core_identification": "Personal trust and reliance upon God/Christ (as instrument of justification)",
  "counter_relation_to_book_core": "SAME_CORE_BROADER (broader label for the same referent)",
  "material_core_denial": "That faith's identity includes being held steady through obedience or that works enact and perfect faith as part of its essence rather than merely evidencing it.

{
  "persuasion": "PERSUADED",
  "support_scope": "FULL",
  "rationale": "The book's core of trusting faithfulness (reliance on the unseen promise held steady through obedience) best unifies the printed texts: emunah's first use as 'steady' hands, Abraham's obedience 'by faith', James's works enacting and perfecting faith, and the explicit denial that works purchase the promise. This outperforms the common trust-as-instrument reading, which must treat the same obedience texts as secondary fruit rather than constitutive of living faith itself, while the book already answers the chief objection by retaining Romans 4 and Ephesians 2.",
  "book_core_identification": "Trusting faithfulness — reliance on God's unseen promise held steady through obedience",
  "book_secondary_elaborations": [
    "Works do not purchase the promise",
    "Works enact and bring faith to maturity",
    "Faith without works is dead"
  ],
  "strongest_counter_interpretation": "Faith primarily denotes personal trust and confident reliance upon God/Christ as the instrument of justification and salvation; works are the necessary subsequent fruit or evidence of genuine (living) faith but are not constitutive of faith itself and do not enact or perfect it.",
  "counter_core_identification": "Personal trust/reliance upon God and Christ (distinct from works as instrument of justification)",
  "counter_relation_to_book_core": "CONTRADICTS",
  "material_core_denial": "That the identity of faith itself includes being held steady through obedience, or that works enact and bring faith to maturity rather than merely evidencing a prior, complete trust.",
  "counter_case": [
    "Hebrews 11:1 defines faith as assurance of things hoped for and conviction of things not seen, without reference to works or obedience",
    "Romans 4:4-5 and Ephesians 2:8-9 explicitly set faith over against works for justification/salvation",
    "The classic reading of James 2 treats 'faith without works is dead' as distinguishing living from dead faith, where true faith produces works as fruit",
    "Lexical and confessional consensus treats pistis chiefly as trust/belief/fiducia, with faithfulness as a related but secondary sense",
    "Many NT contexts present faith as receiving/hearing the gospel message prior to or apart from enumerated works"
  ],
  "book_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Grounds Habakkuk 2:4 in the first biblical occurrence of emunah as 'steady' (Exodus 17:12)",
    "Incorporates Hebrews 11:8 ('by faith Abraham... obeyed') directly into the definition rather than as mere illustration",
    "Takes James 2:22 at face value: faith 'wrought with' works and was 'made perfect' by them",
    "Retains the non-purchase of the promise (Romans 4:4-5; Ephesians 2:8-9) while integrating Ephesians 2:10 and James without contradiction",
    "Coheres with the already-accepted prior finding on belief (receiving testimony that submits) and the chapter's four distinct offices of one covenant response"
  ],
  "counter_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Preserves a sharper distinction between the instrument of justification and its results, matching classic sola fide formulations",
    "Fits numerous contexts in which faith is simply believing the apostolic testimony (e.g., Romans 10:17; John 20:31)",
    "Avoids any risk of appearing to make human obedience co-constitutive of saving faith"
  ],
  "evidence_book_core_cannot_explain": [],
  "comparative_winner": "BOOK",
  "decisive_sources": [
    "Exodus 17:12 (emunah as steady)",
    "Habakkuk 2:4",
    "Hebrews 11:1, 8",
    "James 2:17, 22",
    "Romans 4:4-5",
    "Ephesians 2:8-10",
    "books/symbolic-language/06-knowing-faith-love-and-belief.adoc"
  ],
  "unresolved_objections": [
    "How the definition interacts with confessional 'faith alone' language that keeps works strictly subsequent",
    "Whether every NT occurrence of pistis carries the full 'trusting faithfulness through obedience' sense",
    "The ongoing scholarly debate over pistis Christou (faithfulness of Christ vs. faith in Christ)"
  ],
  "confidence": "high"
}
